metadata.Name: FQuAD2.0
metadata.Description: FQuAD2.0 is a French Question Answering dataset that extends FQuAD1.1 with over 17,000 adversarially hand-crafted unanswerable questions. It is designed for training models that can not only answer questions but also determine when no answer is present in the context, totaling almost 80,000 questions.
metadata.Paper Title: FQuAD2.0: French Question Answering and knowing that you know nothing
metadata.Venue Title: Proceedings of the 2020 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
metadata.Abstract: In 2020, the first French Question Answering dataset, FQuAD1.1, was introduced. With 60,000+ question-answer pairs, it enabled the development of QA models surpassing the human performance in the Reading Comprehension task. However, the obtained models suffered from an important weakness, as they were trained to consistently find an answer to the specified question by reading the associated context. In real-life applications however, it is often the case that asked questions do not have an answer in the associated context. To overcome this difficulty, we introduce FQuAD2.0, which extends FQuAD1.1 with 17,000+ unanswerable questions, hand-crafted to be difficult to distinguish from answerable questions, making it the first French adversarial Question Answering dataset with a grand total of almost 80,000 questions. We provide a study of the impact of the number of adversarial questions used for training on the performance of CamemBERT models. We also study how multilingual models fine-tuned solely on question-answer pairs of a single language (English), performs in another language (French). We also take interest in performances of such models trained on both French and English datasets.
